To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extinction-coredcted [OII]/ Halpha ratio is a good indicator of the oxygen abundance of emission line galaxies, and that it depends on the metallicity and ionization states of interstellar gas.
the [OII]/(Halpha+ [NII]) ratio depends on the metallicity, and for metal-poor galaxies it also depends on the excitation state of the interstellar medium.
the [OII]/ Halpha ratio is a strong function of metallicity and excitation state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the [OII]/Ha flux ratio and the physical properties of galaxies.
the systematic variation of [OII] emission in galaxies and its relationship to the physical parameters of the interstellar medium.
the relationship between the [OII]/(Halpha + [NII]) and [OIII]/(Hbeta + [OIII]) line ratios and the metallicity of the gas phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the [OII]/(Halpha) line ratio of emission-line galaxies depends on the metallicity of the interstellar medium.
the [OII]/(Halpha+Hbeta) flux ratio is a good metallicity indicator for galaxies with metallicity 12+log (O/H)> 8.4 and a poor indicator for galaxies with lower metallicity.
the extinction-correted [OII]/(Halpha) ratio depends on the metallicity, redding, and excitation level of the gas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for metal-poor galaxies the extinction-correct [OII] emission line is a good indicator of the gas-phase metallicity.
the [OII]/ Halpha ratio is a good indicator of the gas-phase oxygen abundances, and the ionization state of interstellar gas in the metal-poor galaxy regime, but not in the metal-rich regime.

for a given metallicity, the extinction-correct [OII] flux relative to the Halpha flux is a good indicator of the ionization state of the gas in galaxies, but the relationship between the extinction-c-corrected [OI]/Halpha ratio and the gas-phase oxygen metallicity is more complicated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extinction-correction procedure is crucial for the determination of the metallicity from the R_{23}-based metallicity calibration.
the [OII]/Ha ratio of galaxies is not only a function of the metallicity, but also of their excitation state and reddening.
, for the first time, the [OII]/Ha ratio is correlated with oxygen abundance for a sample of galaxies covering a wide range of metallicity.
